chapters.title: Chapter 1: The World's Stock Markets at a Glance

lessons.title: Why Every Indian Investor Should Understand Global Markets

children.text: On Monday, 7 April 2025, Indian investors saw a sea of red before NSE even opened. The week before, US President Donald Trump had announced sweeping tariffs on 2 April, and US stocks had suffered their worst two-day fall since 2020. By the time the Nifty opened at 9:15 am, Tokyo had been falling for nearly four hours and Hong Kong for more than two. Nothing had changed inside India over the weekend. No RBI decision, no earnings shock, no policy change. Yet the Nifty closed 3.24% lower. If you only watch Indian markets, days like this feel random. If you watch the world, you can see them coming.

body.text: India is one market in a connected world. Global money, global earnings and global mood reach your Indian portfolio every trading day, whether or not you ever buy a single foreign share.

body.caption: One Monday, four markets: closing levels on 7 April 2025

cells: -13.2%, its worst day since the 1997 Asian crisis

body.text: Look again at the table. India fell hard, but far less than Hong Kong or Tokyo. Investors judged India less exposed to US tariffs than export-heavy economies like Japan and China. Connected does not mean identical. Understanding global markets is as much about knowing where India differs as where it follows.

children.text: India Is a Small Slice of a Very Big Pie

markDefs.definition: The total value of a company's shares, calculated as share price multiplied by shares outstanding. Add it up for every listed company in a country and you get that country's market cap.

The MSCI All Country World Index. A widely tracked benchmark of large and mid-sized listed companies across developed and emerging markets. Global funds use it to decide how much money each country gets.

children.text: It is easy to feel that the Nifty is the centre of the financial universe when it dominates every business channel in India. It is not. Add up the
market capitalisation
of every listed company on earth and you get roughly $160 trillion. India's share is about 3%. The United States alone makes up more than 60% of the
MSCI ACWI
, the index most global fund managers measure themselves against. When the biggest pool of money in the world moves, a 3% market does not get a vote. It gets carried along.

body.caption: How to calculate any country's slice of the global pie

body.title: Find India's slice
body.prompt: Global listed equity is worth about $160 trillion and India's market cap is about $4.9 trillion. What is India's share of world market capitalisation, in percent? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: India's share = $4.9 trillion ÷ $160 trillion × 100 = 3.06%, which rounds to 3.1%. For every $100 invested in listed shares worldwide, only about $3 sits in Indian companies. That is why decisions made in New York, London and Tokyo can move the Nifty more than decisions made in Mumbai on some days.

children.text: Three Ways the World Reaches Your Portfolio

Global markets do not affect Indian stocks by magic. They travel through three clear channels: money, earnings and mood. Once you can name the channel, you can judge how big the impact is likely to be and how long it might last.

body.caption: The three channels at a glance
headers: How it shows up in India

cells: Foreign funds shifting capital between countries
FPI buying or selling of large caps, rupee moves
Demand from customers in the US, Europe and Asia
Revenue and profit growth of IT, pharma and auto exporters
Overnight moves in US and Asian indices
Gap-up or gap-down openings, GIFT Nifty signals

children.text: Channel 1: Money

markDefs.definition: Foreign Portfolio Investors. Overseas funds and institutions registered with SEBI that buy listed Indian shares, bonds and other securities.
The MSCI Emerging Markets Index. A benchmark of large and mid-sized companies across about 24 emerging economies, including China, Taiwan, South Korea, India and Brazil.

children.text: Most foreign money in Indian shares comes from
FPIs
. Many of them do not pick India first. They pick an index, usually the
MSCI EM

index, and then hold each country roughly in line with its weight. So India's slice of foreign money depends not just on how India performs, but on how Taiwan, Korea and China perform too. When chip stocks in Taipei and Seoul rallied on AI demand in 2025 and 2026, their weights rose and India's shrank automatically.

body.label: India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index
body.context: Down from nearly 21% in September 2024. Taiwan has overtaken China as the largest country in the index, and India now ranks fourth.

body.title: When the index shrinks India
body.prompt: A global emerging markets fund manages $50 billion and holds India exactly at its MSCI EM index weight. India's weight falls from 21% to 12%, and the fund's total size stays the same. How much money, in $ billion, must the fund pull out of Indian shares?
body.explanation: At 21%, the fund holds $50 billion × 21% = $10.5 billion in India. At 12%, it holds $50 billion × 12% = $6 billion. The difference is $10.5 billion minus $6 billion = $4.5 billion. At USD/INR 95, that is over ₹42,000 crore of selling from a single fund, even though nothing went wrong with Indian companies.

body.text: Do not read every FPI sell-off as a vote against India. A shrinking index weight, rising US bond yields or a hot rally in another market can all trigger selling. Always ask what changed abroad before concluding something is wrong at home.

children.text: Channel 2: Earnings

Many Nifty companies are Indian by listing but global by revenue. Infosys earns more than half its revenue from North America, and TCS close to half. A US bank that cuts its technology budget shows up in their order books months later. Sun Pharma and Dr. Reddy's sell generic medicines in the US. Tata Motors' passenger vehicle business owns Jaguar Land Rover, which sells mainly in the UK, Europe, the US and China. When those economies slow, these Indian stocks feel it directly, through their profit and loss statements.

body.title: Spot the global earner
body.question: News breaks that US companies are sharply cutting technology spending ahead of a possible recession. Which Nifty 50 stock is most directly exposed through its earnings?
body.explanation: Infosys earns more than half its revenue from North America, largely from technology spending by US companies. Hindustan Unilever sells soap and food in India, Power Grid earns regulated returns on Indian transmission lines, and SBI lends mostly within India. All four can fall on a bad global day through the mood channel, but only Infosys takes a direct hit to its earnings.

children.text: Channel 3: Mood and the Overnight Relay

markDefs.definition: A US dollar-denominated Nifty 50 futures contract listed on NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) at GIFT City, Gujarat. It trades for about 21 hours a day, so it reflects global news while NSE is closed.

children.text: Stock markets pass the baton around the globe like a relay race. Asia trades first, Europe picks up in India's afternoon, and the US trades while India sleeps. Whatever happens in New York overnight is already priced into Tokyo by early morning and into
GIFT Nifty

before NSE opens. This is why the Nifty so often opens with a gap up or gap down. The mood channel is fast, but it is also the one most likely to reverse within days if nothing changes in the money or earnings channels.

body.title: Why these timings shift by an hour in winter

children.text: United States.
Daylight saving ends on the first Sunday of November (1 November 2026). New York then opens at 8:00 pm IST and closes at 2:30 am IST.
United Kingdom and Europe.
Clocks go back on the last Sunday of October (25 October 2026). London, Paris and Frankfurt then open at 1:30 pm IST.
Asia and India.
Japan, China, Hong Kong and India do not use daylight saving, so Tokyo, Hong Kong and Shanghai open at the same IST times all year.

body.title: The early bird market
body.textWithBlank: Tokyo opens at 5:30 am IST, which is 3 hours and ___ minutes before NSE's 9:15 am open.
body.explanation: From 5:30 am to 9:15 am is 3 hours and 45 minutes. That is a long head start. By the time Indian markets open, Tokyo has already digested the full US session and nearly half of its own trading day.

children.text: Your Portfolio Is Already More Global Than You Think

Even if you have never opened a US brokerage account, you probably own global exposure. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, one of India's largest equity funds, has for years held US stocks such as Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. NSE lists ETFs like the Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 ETF (MON100) and the Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF, which you can buy on Zerodha like any Indian share. And your Nifty index fund carries IT and pharma exporters whose fortunes depend on customers abroad. The question is not whether you are exposed to global markets. It is whether you know how much.

body.text: Indian mutual funds cannot send unlimited money abroad. RBI and SEBI cap overseas investment by the entire mutual fund industry at $7 billion. When that limit gets close, fund houses pause fresh investments into their international funds. This is why some Indian US-focused funds and ETFs have at times traded at a premium to their underlying value.

body.title: Audit your own global exposure in 15 minutes
steps: Open the latest monthly factsheet of each equity mutual fund you own and look for a foreign or overseas equity section.
Check your holdings in Zerodha Console or Kite and list every ETF that tracks a foreign index, such as MON100.
Mark every direct stock holding in IT services, pharma exports or auto companies with large overseas sales.
For your two largest exporter holdings, open screener.in and check the annual report for the share of revenue earned outside India.
Write down a rough percentage of your portfolio that depends on money, earnings or mood from abroad. Revisit it as you finish this course.

body.title: A bad night in New York
body.scenario: It is a Friday in September. At 6:00 pm IST, a much weaker than expected US jobs report is released. By 9:00 pm IST, the Nasdaq is down 3% on recession fears, and the US dollar is weakening. You hold four things: Infosys shares, HDFC Bank shares, units of the Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 ETF (MON100) and Hindustan Unilever shares. Indian markets are shut until Monday morning.
body.prompt: For each holding, name the channel through which the US news reaches it and how strongly. Then list what you would check on Monday morning before 9:15 am.
body.modelAnswer:
1. MON100: The most direct hit. It tracks the Nasdaq 100, so the ETF's underlying value falls with the US index. A weaker dollar can also shave off a little more in rupee terms. Expect it to open lower on NSE on Monday.
2. Infosys: Hit through the earnings channel. US recession fears raise doubts about technology budgets of its North American clients, and Nifty IT stocks usually react on the next open.
3. HDFC Bank: Hit mainly through the mood and money channels. Its earnings are domestic, but FPIs own a large share of it and may sell in a risk-off move.
4. Hindustan Unilever: The least exposed. Its earnings are domestic and defensive. It may dip on a weak open but can even hold up well as money rotates into safer stocks.

On Monday morning, check: how the Nasdaq and S&P 500 closed on Friday, the Nikkei after 5:30 am, GIFT Nifty after 6:30 am, the rupee's likely opening level, and Friday's FPI flow data. Then decide whether this is a one-day mood shock or the start of an earnings story.

children.text: What This Course Will Give You

This is not a course on how to buy foreign shares. It is a course on how to read the world's markets the way a professional does, so that the Nifty makes more sense. The rest of Chapter 1 maps the world's biggest exchanges and explains how index providers classify countries. Chapters 2, 3 and 4 take you through the US, Europe and Asia one region at a time: their exchanges, indices, rules and personalities. Chapter 5 puts them side by side on valuations, growth and currencies, and ends with a simple dashboard you can check every morning before NSE opens.

points: India is about 3% of world market capitalisation. The US makes up about 62.5% of the MSCI ACWI, so global money moves are driven mostly by what happens outside India.
Global markets reach your portfolio through three channels: money (FPI flows), earnings (exporters' overseas revenue) and mood (overnight index moves).
India's MSCI EM weight fell from nearly 21% to about 12% between September 2024 and August 2026, forcing index-linked funds to hold less India even when nothing was wrong at home.
Infosys, TCS, Sun Pharma and Jaguar Land Rover's parent all earn heavily abroad, so global slowdowns hit their earnings directly.
Tokyo opens at 5:30 am IST, GIFT Nifty at 6:30 am and New York at 7:00 pm, so global news is priced in long before NSE opens at 9:15 am.
On 7 April 2025 the Nifty fell 3.24% while Hong Kong fell 13.2%. Markets are connected, but not identical.
Most Indian investors already hold global exposure through flexi cap funds, foreign index ETFs and exporter stocks.
